body:
Source: GitHub issue #816 (bug, P1-high). Re-verified on main @ 6bf8841c: plugins/adlc-cursor/rails-checker.mjs — `MUTATING_TOOL_HINTS` (line 32) is a SUBSTRING match list including 'write' and 'create'; `PURE_READS` (lines 49-53) is a Set of EXACT normalized tokens including 'globsearch'/'filesearch'/'fetch' but NOT the combined tokens Cursor actually emits. `classifyTool()` (line ~101) checks mutating hints FIRST (substring), then PURE_READS (exact), else 'other'. `decide()` in plugins/adlc-cursor/hooks/adlc-rails-guard.mjs (~line 200-245) denies any tool classified 'mutating' OR ('other' AND not a recognized shell tool) when it carries no inspectable file path, under active P4 enforcement.

Confirmed via direct import of classifyTool: `todo_write` normalizes to 'todowrite' -> contains 'write' -> 'mutating' -> denied. `create_diagram` normalizes to 'creatediagram' -> contains 'create' -> 'mutating' -> denied. `glob_file_search` normalizes to 'globfilesearch' -> not in PURE_READS (only has 'globsearch') -> 'other' -> denied (opaque, no path, not shell). `fetch_pull_request` normalizes to 'fetchpullrequest' -> not in PURE_READS (only has 'fetch') -> 'other' -> denied. None of these four tools take a file-path argument, so they can never satisfy the has-a-path exemption either — they are ALWAYS denied whenever ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 and a ticket is active, regardless of what the agent is doing. The issue documents this pushes operators to disable enforcement entirely to get work done, which silently removes the gate for everything, not just these four tools — the actual consequence is worse than the four individual denials.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package: plugins/adlc-cursor. rails-checker.mjs already has a precedent for exactly this shape of fix: `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES` (line ~66) is an EXACT whole-normalized-name Set (not substring) specifically because — per its own doc comment — a substring/token predicate would let a novel structured mutator like `terminal_modify` slip through as exempt. `isShellTool()` checks it before the opaque-mutator branch fires. Follow this exact precedent, do not invent a different shape. Tests: `node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/*.test.mjs` from the worktree root. plugins/adlc-cursor/test/rails-guard.test.mjs is the primary existing test file for `decide()`/`classifyTool()`; add new tests there. Do not touch `packages/core/lib/shell.mjs` or any other harness's classifier — this file has its OWN independent classifier (not the shared shell-command one; it classifies structured TOOL NAMES, a different axis).

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. Add `'globfilesearch'` and `'fetchpullrequest'` to `PURE_READS` (both are read-only whole-token names Cursor actually emits) — the simplest, lowest-risk part of the fix; these belong in the SAME `readonly` classification tier the existing exact-token entries already use.
2. Add a new EXACT whole-normalized-name Set, e.g. `NON_MUTATING_STRUCTURED_TOOL_NAMES` (mirroring `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`'s pattern and its documented rationale), seeded with `'todowrite'` and `'creatediagram'` — Cursor first-party tools verified to never carry a file-mutation argument. Consult it in `classifyTool()` BEFORE the `MUTATING_TOOL_HINTS` substring check (so 'todowrite' short-circuits to 'readonly' or an equivalent exempt classification before 'write' can match it as a substring), exactly the same ordering discipline `isShellTool()` already uses relative to the opaque-mutator branch in `decide()`. Do NOT make this a substring/heuristic list — exact whole-name only, same reasoning as `SHELL_TOOL_NAMES`'s own comment: a heuristic here would risk exempting a genuine future mutator whose name happens to contain 'todo' or 'diagram'.
3. `MUTATING_TOOL_HINTS`-driven substring matching must remain the FIRST-and-fail-closed check for every tool NOT on the two new exact-name additions above — this ticket narrows four specific, verified-safe false positives, it does not weaken the substring-match fail-closed default for anything else. A genuinely novel/unrecognized mutating-shaped tool name must still deny exactly as today.
4. Per the issue's own recommendation, pin the current Cursor tool-name inventory this ticket relies on (todo_write, create_diagram, glob_file_search, fetch_pull_request, plus the existing web_search/read_file/list_dir/run_terminal_cmd controls) in a table-driven test, so a future Cursor tool rename is caught by a failing test rather than silently reopening this bug.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 `classifyTool('todo_write')` and `classifyTool('create_diagram')` no longer classify as 'mutating'; both allow under `decide()` with ADLC_P4_ENFORCEMENT=1 and an active ticket, with no file path supplied. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/rails-guard.test.mjs`
- AC2 `classifyTool('glob_file_search')` and `classifyTool('fetch_pull_request')` classify as 'readonly'; both allow under the same conditions. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/rails-guard.test.mjs`
- AC3 Table-driven regression pinning ALL of: todo_write, create_diagram, glob_file_search, fetch_pull_request -> allow; web_search, read_file, list_dir, run_terminal_cmd -> allow (already correct, must stay correct); a synthetic novel mutating-shaped tool name (e.g. `terminal_modify` or similar, NOT on either new exact-name list) with no path -> still denies. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/rails-guard.test.mjs`
- AC4 A genuine rail-target structured edit (real file path under a frozen rail) still denies exactly as before — this ticket must not touch the has-a-path decision path. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/rails-guard.test.mjs`
- AC5 Existing suite green. verify: `node --test plugins/adlc-cursor/test/*.test.mjs`
- AC6 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0 (also run `--max 80` once locally before review)

OUT OF SCOPE: SHELL_TOOL_NAMES and the shell-exemption path (already correct). Any other harness's tool classifier (this is cursor-only; #809 is the copilot analog, being fixed in a separate ticket/PR). Changing the substring-match design for MUTATING_TOOL_HINTS itself — only additive exact-name exemptions, per NORMATIVE #3.
title: adlc-cursor: stop denying no-path first-party tools (todo_write, create_diagram, glob/fetch variants) under P4 enforcement
